items.criterion: Every question uses the fallback layout: a bold `**Question N of T · Label**` heading, the question, 2-4 options as a bulleted `**X · label**: sentence` list, and one `Reply …` hint line, with no code block or box drawing.
Each option has one sentence saying what it does and why it fits this request, ending on its cost or trade-off.
The rhythm holds: each answer gets a one-line echo in one of the exact forms, at the top of the message that carries the next question.

After the last answer the skill shows a bulleted list with one echo line per question and asks for confirmation in one sentence; once confirmed, it says what it will do in one short paragraph before doing the work.
No assistant message contains more than one question.
A question marks at most one option `(recommended)`, lists it first, and only when something the user said points to it, which its sentence names; with nothing to go on, no option is marked.
The quiz commits to its question list up front: the total T stays the same from the first question to the last and matches the questions asked, and it is no more than about seven.

Each echo records what the user actually replied, in the matching exact form: the choice, any note, `(you decided: recommended)` or `(you decided: first option)` for a deferral, `(from: "…")` for words matched to an option.
No question, echo or resolved list is wrapped in a code block or drawn with box-drawing characters, and no emojis appear outside sample content.
The questions asked are the ones whose answers would materially change the work for this request, most load-bearing first, and none re-asks something the prompt already settled.
Each question's options are realistic, distinct choices for this request, and any recommendation fits what the user said.
The paragraph before the work and the work itself reflect every resolved answer and note, so the user gets what they chose.
